stem: A school has exactly \$9,000 to spend on desks that cost \$450 each and chairs that cost \$150 each. The graph of \(450x + 150y = 9{,}000\) in the \(xy\)-plane shows the combinations of \(x\) desks and \(y\) chairs the school can buy with all of the money. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the \(x\)-intercept of the graph?

choices.A: If the school buys no desks, it can buy 60 chairs.
choices.B: If the school buys no desks, it can buy 20 chairs.
choices.C: If the school buys no chairs, it can buy 20 desks.
choices.D: Each desk costs 20 times as much as each chair.

solution: At the \(x\)-intercept, \(y = 0\), so no chairs are bought.
Then \(450x = 9{,}000\) and \(x = 20\): the money buys 20 desks.

explanation.B: Incorrect. The \(x\)-intercept has \(y = 0\), so it is the number of desks, not chairs, when no chairs are bought.
explanation.C: Correct. At the \(x\)-intercept, \(y = 0\): \(450x = 9{,}000\), so \(x = 20\) desks and 0 chairs.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The intercept is a count of desks; a desk costs 3 times as much as a chair.

verify:
x = symbols('x')
assert solve(Eq(450*x, 9000), x) == [20]
assert choices[answer] == 'If the school buys no chairs, it can buy 20 desks.'
